purpose: Test whether the frozen Stage72 constraint-native receptor-selection objective becomes classically nontrivial when k grows beyond three, before constructing an explicit variable-k CQM or using cloud or quantum hardware.

larger_k_workloads.quality_threshold_rule: For each model and k, use exact integer subset-sum dynamic programming to choose the smallest deficit threshold containing at least ceil(density*choose(n,k)) subsets. Equal-deficit boundary states are all retained, so realized density may be slightly larger.
larger_k_workloads.nonexact_reference_rule: For cells above the exact limit, use the best objective found by all frozen methods and repeats, label it pooled_best_known, and never call it a global optimum.

solver_protocol.initialization_rule: Random fixed-k subsets are drawn uniformly until the exact quality threshold is met; attempts are reported separately from the matched swap-proposal budget. A deterministic lowest-deficit fallback is permitted only after the frozen maximum attempts.
solver_protocol.neighborhood: one selected receptor out and one unselected receptor in, preserving cardinality exactly; quality feasibility is checked before objective evaluation
solver_protocol.decision_metric: matched swap-proposal counts and mean pair-redundancy objective; wall-clock runtime is excluded from route decisions

benchmark_gate.interpretation: Scale, exact-small-instance validity, and nonexact solver disagreement authorize only an explicit variable-k CQM design. Annealing competitiveness additionally authorizes a local hardware-shaped sampler PoC, but neither gate authorizes direct QPU execution or quantum claims.

interpretation_boundary: Stage74 is a post-hoc optimization-scaling diagnostic on four consumed historical development targets. It reuses frozen pair and quality coefficients, does not select a biologically optimal k, and does not measure screening efficacy, independent-target generalization, certified global optima above the enumeration limit, physical embedding, cloud-hybrid speed, QPU performance, quantum scaling, or quantum advantage.
